Every data-driven claim on this site is backed by code that can be run and checked.
Reproducibility is the first principle here: a result isn't a finding until someone
else can reproduce it.

## This website
The full source for davidmaguire.ai is public and built with Quarto:
[github.com/davidolivermaguire-ai/davidmaguire.ai](https://github.com/davidolivermaguire-ai/davidmaguire.ai)

## Research code
Each [Quant Research Lab](quant-lab/index.qmd) experiment links to its own

## market-state-lab
A purpose-built benchmark harness for the proposal's
[RQ1](phd/index.qmd) — *which methods most reliably identify market state out of sample?*
Because that is a **comparative** question, the deliverable is a protocol rather than a model:
one point-in-time data layer, one shared feature set, a pluggable estimator interface, one
walk-forward engine, and one metrics suite, so that nine methods compete on identical terms.

It currently implements four transparent baselines, a Kalman local-linear-trend filter, a
Gaussian HMM, a Markov-switching regression, and CUSUM and BOCPD change-point detectors, scored
across four tiers: recovery on synthetic markets with known regimes, stability, timeliness, and
[decision value against a volatility-only benchmark](quant-lab/state-decision-value/index.qmd).
Every estimator must pass an automated look-ahead test asserting that its estimate at time *t*
is unchanged when future data is appended — filtered, never smoothed.

The harness is being prepared for public release; until then the experiments it produces are
written up in full, with every parameter and number stated, in the Quant Lab.

## Principles
- **Reproducibility first** — code is published alongside the result it produces.
- **Versioned** — everything is tracked in Git, so results can be traced to the exact code that generated them.
- **Honest** — the code shows the full method, including the parts that didn't work.
